name: Garlic
grown_as: Garlic, grown from single cloves planted in autumn or winter and lifted the next summer as a bulb of many cloves. William's is a softneck, which seldom flowers. Hardneck garlic sends up a flower stem (scape) in June of the same season, not in a second year, so the 'In flower (year 2)' drawing follows hardneck garlic. ⚠️ CHECK: the stage label, and whether a softneck needs a flower drawing at all.
habit: A single upright false stem of wrapped leaf sheaths 30 to 60 cm, with flat leaves set alternately in two ranks up it. Hardnecks then send a stiff scape up through the middle that loops once or twice before straightening, ending in a beaked head.

leaf.arrangement: Alternate in two ranks up the false stem, each leaf rising from inside the one below
leaf.outline: Long flat strap, 20 to 45 cm by 1 to 2.5 cm, tapering gradually to the tip
leaf.base: A long sheath forming the false stem
leaf.surface: Flat or folded slightly along a keel, SOLID not hollow, smooth with a waxy bloom

flower.form: A small round head of tiny bulbils mixed with a few small star-shaped flowers, inside a long papery beaked spathe
flower.colour: Whitish-pink to pale purple, often green-tinged; many flowers wither in bud
flower.centre: Six stamens, not sticking out far
flower.behind: A papery spathe drawn out into a long thin beak 7 to 15 cm, wrapping the head, splitting and staying attached on one side
flower.carried: In a small umbel at the top of the scape, the flowers on long thin stalks above a cluster of purplish-green bulbils
flower.size: Flowers 3 to 5 mm; head 3 to 5 cm

fruit: Seldom any seed. The head ripens into a cluster of small bulbils like tiny cloves, which can be planted.
winter: Autumn-planted cloves make a few short upright leaves 10 to 20 cm that stay green through winter.

leaf: a long flat strap, keeled, solid not hollow
parallel veins, no teeth, tapering to a long point
bloom: a small head of pinkish-white flowers mixed with small bulbils
a long papery beak from the spathe
clove: a single curved wedge-shaped clove with a pointed tip
a flat root plate at the base and a papery skin
young: a single upright stem of flat leaves in two ranks
crop: a round bulb of several cloves wrapped in white papery skin, sometimes purple-streaked
lower leaves brown, upper ones still green
flower: a scape that loops once before straightening, rising through the leaves
a beaked spathe at its tip
seedhead: a dry head of small bulbils, the spathe split and papery

look_alikes: Leek has broader flat leaves fanned in one plane and no cloves. Elephant garlic is a leek with large cloves and a big lilac flower head. Wild garlic has broad soft leaves on stalks. Three-cornered leek has a three-angled stem and nodding white bells.
